body:
If people are interested I have a work around.

---

The idea is to have a separate viewport to hold the particles. My workflow has:

1. A viewport with full resolution for HD textures
2. A sub viewport scaled 4x with 2D transform pixel snapping to true, this is where the whole game is, called `SubViewport`
3. A second sub viewport without 2D transform pixel snapping, called `ShadowSubViewport`

In `ShadowSubViewport` I have a single `Node2D` which I call `ShadowPlayer`. The script for this node is simple:

```gdscript
class_name PlayerShadow
extends Node2D

func _ready() -> void:
    GameManager.register_shadow(self)

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
    # Follow the player
    global_position = GameManager.player.global_position

    # Ensure the shadow viewport follows the main game viewport
    var main_vp = GameManager.player.get_viewport()
    get_viewport().canvas_transform = main_vp.canvas_transform
```

Then, the player, which is a child of `SubViewport` has the following "hack":

```gdscript
func _send_particles_to_shadow() -> void:
	for child in GameManager.shadow.get_children():
		child.queue_free()

	for child in particles.get_children():
		if not child is GPUParticles2D:
			continue
		particles.remove_child(child)
		GameManager.shadow.add_child(child)
``` 

The idea here is that the player has all the particles and information but when the player is introduced into the tree we move every particle (held in a particles `Node2D` just for organisation) and reparent them to the Shadow

Now, the particles move with the player, but in a sub viewport without the snapping, avoiding the jitter bug.

author: yikescloud

body:
> I would fully expect all physics callbacks to stop entirely once the program begins to quit

To a common misconception these signals are NOT physics callbacks.

They are just Area2D Node internal bookkeeping lists of overlaps getting updated. Some entries in that bookkeeping list may get updated after a real physics server sync but many are also just caused by signal-spaghettification with other Node objects and them changing tree and shape status.

So this here is a normal Node "leave" routine, to be more specific the Area2D node cleaning up its internal bookkeeping list of overlaps and emitting the related signals. Has nothing to do with the actual physics. If the entire SceneTree is tearing down all its Nodes follow their normal exit routine that just happens in whatever node order.

A signal can emit at any time, it is not bound to a Node or a Node being in a SceneTree. That some Nodes may not emit their signals while not inside the SceneTree is their own custom code but not a default behavior of signals so you can not expect that.

The example is using unsafe code in a signal callback that needs to be fixed. E.g. by doing a sanity check on objects before they are used. In the example any situation the node would be connected manual to the PhysicsServer callback but still outside the tree the script would also crash. Writing safe code so it does not crash on null objects is not a responsibility the engine can take away from users.
author: smix8

body:
Would this be a documentation issue then? This distinction in behavior doesn't seem to be very clear (in fact, the "Consider using signals instead" line at the end of the documentation for the overlap list access functions makes it sound like the signals are more directly integrated into the physics callbacks rather than using the area's overlap list.)  That Area2D emits body_exited upon being removed (regardless of said removal being due to a quit or not) also seems unintuitive to me.

Also, I'd note that in the vast majority of cases where a node is outside the scene tree, it's because the node was removed from or created outside the tree explicitly by the programmer. There is no reason in normal operation to ever believe that a node has unpredictably left the scene tree, hence a sanity check on get_tree() not being intuitively necessary. The tree getting cleaned up during quit is very much a special case in this sense.
author: Nevermind3476

body:
> Would this be a documentation issue then?

I have no good answer to that. I leave it to the documentation guys to decide. It is a delicate problem to solve to not only to find the right place where to add something to documentation but also find the right balance between too much or too little information.


As a general hint for safe dealing with signal callbacks that have external dependencies they should all be treated as if it is a static function. In the example turning the callback function into static would have immediately thrown and error on `get_tree()` revealing that that function is complete unsafe to be used in a signal context without a null check. The tree object is neither a static object or a singleton, so the engine can make zero guarantees that that object always exists in context of a signal callback.

body:
`\0` is technically a valid unicode string; however Godot currently doesn't handle it correctly since some of its own APIs assume strings are `\0` free and additionally `\0` terminated.
I've been slowly addressing this problem since 2 years; some of my fixes involved printing more errors to avoid worse bugs down the line.

In other words, Godot is currently incapable of handling a `char(0)` correctly right now, so the call itself errors and produces a length one string with the replacement character instead.
author: Ivorforce

body:
> For context, seems like GDScript tries to compile time eval some functions. The lack of proper error propagation makes it basically impossible to handle errors during that though.

For this particular case, we could modify the condition or add a separate check here (if it is expected that `char(0)` might become valid someday):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec67cbe92628bdaf979b10594359ba6f02cf8838/modules/gdscript/gdscript_utility_functions.cpp#L120-L126

Unfortunately in general, but fortunately in situations like this, GDScript can perform compile-time calculations in fairly limited cases, so we could take them into account individually.
author: dalexeev

body:
> For this particular case, we could modify the condition or add a separate check here (if it is expected that char(0) might become valid someday)

Changing this to the same condition actual string use probably is a good way to fix error spam. Even if we will support `NUL`s in the string, this check is not correct for the rest of range, should be something like:
```c++
code <= 0 || (code & 0xfffff800) == 0xd800 || code > 0x10ffff
```

body:
Enabling keep y velocity doesn't let the NavigationAgent3D have some grace in its Y position so what ends up happening is that if the agent is far from the NavigationRegion3D it'll internally still try to go up causing the hitches you'll see as the agent tries to go from the middle to the sides.
Disabling it and overriding the y velocity after the fact also doesn't solve it as it'll still slow down on X and Z,

The end result is that you need a really precise NavigationRegion3D and path_height_offset to be able to maintain the velocity that you set on the X and Z.
Without avoidance you can get the array of the path positions and manually allow for some range of grace in the Y position, however if you want to use avoidance you can't do this as far as i know? 

What I'm asking for is either a way to fully allow to ignore the Y position even internally or to allow for some grace on the Y position that way even if the NavigationRegion3D is simple in polygons and not entirely set at the right height your agents will still move accordingly in the X and Z.

(the navigation region on the test has its height slightly up on purpose, being above the height of the character body to show minimally and fast what I'm talking about with keep y velocity)

body:

body:
> push constants no longer have to be padded at the end to a multiple of 16, just a multiple of 4.

This is incorrect. The smallest storage type in GLSL and SPIR-V is one byte (see [GL_EXT_shader_8bit_storage](<https://github.com/KhronosGroup/GLSL/blob/main/extensions/ext/GL_EXT_shader_16bit_storage.txt>), [GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_int8](<https://github.com/KhronosGroup/GLSL/blob/main/extensions/ext/GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types.txt>), [SPV_INTEL_int4](<https://github.khronos.org/SPIRV-Registry/extensions/INTEL/SPV_INTEL_int4.html#_modifications_to_the_spir_v_specification_version_1_6>)), however [Godot only enables 16bit storage](<https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L1452-L1455>) and not [8bit storage](<https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_KHR_8bit_storage.html>).

I.e. the smallest allowed storage type is 2 bytes.
- If you have a type smaller than 2 bytes:
    - If you have validation layers enabled: a validation error should be given.
    - If you do not have validation layers enabled: it might work regardless since modern GPUs support 8bit storage, but it may also fail depending on your GPU and driver.

Regardless, 16bit storage may not be available for certain GPUs and drivers, in which case the smallest allowed storage type is 4 bytes. As far as I'm aware, [there is currently no way of querying support for this](<https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#enum-renderingdevice-features>) so your best bet is to either not use 16 bit types in storage or to just assume there is support for this. Godot does however have a features enum member for 16bit floats, [`RenderingDevice::Features::SUPPORTS_HALF_FLOAT`](<https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/servers/rendering/rendering_device_commons.h#L1025>) ([16bit storage is part of it](<https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L7390>)), and [it is used to check if 16bit floats are available](<https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp#L583>), but [it's not exposed](<https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L9765-L9771>).

Perhaps exposing the `SUPPORTS_HALF_FLOAT` member and updating documentation would be helpful?

Mind you, I have no idea what the situation is like for Direct and Metal.

body:
```
WARNING: Vector3 cannot be normalized, the elements must be finite. Making (0, 0, 0) as a fallback.
     at: normalize (./core/math/vector3.h:551)
```
This is a regression in Godot Physics or Vector3 introduced in 4.7dev3. It is not present in 4.6.3, 4.7dev1, 4.7dev2. It is not a documentation or a plugin issue. In our case it's triggered by NANs in the vertices of a HeightmapShape to punch holes in the collision. It affects move_and_slide() and raycasts.

Quick test: Download Terrain3D from the asset lib, turn right 90 degrees, fly towards the mountain and into the cave.

edit:
Most likely caused by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116427
This adds a warning which causes the error spam and kills engine performance.
Either Godot Physics should not try to normalize nans, or Vector3 should not dump spam onto the console.

body:
I suspect this is more strictly on the editor side when I look closer.

The detach operation is handled here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec67cbe92628bdaf979b10594359ba6f02cf8838/editor/docks/scene_tree_dock.cpp#L848-L864

Which will set the script to the parent script, this in turn is handled here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec67cbe92628bdaf979b10594359ba6f02cf8838/core/object/object.cpp#L978-L994

Which removes the script instance, which should erase the custom data entirely when assigning

I think the solution here, at least on the editor side, is to track all the properties from the parent script and making sure to assign them after the swap

It might be possible to handle it core side but I'm not sure switching the script fundamentally is safe, but it might be an issue with that

So in summary, one of two things need to be done here:
* Either make sure the editor tracks properties from the parent script, or
* Make sure that assigning the script for an object to a parent script of the current script preserves properties

body: I looked into this a bit. I was able to reproduce the behavior with the MRP and it looks like Windows specifically dislikes multiple shift keys with the KEYUP event. If multiple shift keys are pressed only the last KEYUP will fire. So previously there was an edge case put in for if there's still a shift key pressed fire the KEYUP anyway. This worked for when one shift was released after another, but when both are released simultaneously there isn't a shift being pressed for the edge case, and Windows still only fires one KEYUP event. I made a pull request #120327 that would change all shift up cases to checking raw keyboard input instead, so we wouldn't have to depend on Windows KEYUP.

body:
why would you want this? then autoload scenes wouldnt be able to use those resources, and the only "upside" to this would be that you could abuse the hell out of autoload scenes for what clearly should be the job of something - *anything* - else. the solution here is obvious: dont access the autoload from before its loaded.

if you want a singleton, make an actual singleton, eg using `static`. not an additional main scene with a global name. if you want projectsettings, use projectsettings. not an additional main scene with a global name. it's not hard not to abuse autoloads for everything.
author: nonchip

body:
Autoloads exist to be global singletons within, primarily, the scope of the scenetree. The further you stray from that, the more likely you will be burned.

This is a consequence of bad architecture, not a problem to be solved. Resources are already not really supposed to have references into the scenetree, much less a global instance. I assure you, godot is not so completely incompetent that your hand is twisted in this scenario. I am confident there is a way to accomplish your goals in a manner far less inane.
author: UwUMacaroniTime

body:
@nonchip @UwUMacaroniTime  

This problem goes beyond `ResourceFormatLoaders` and `ResourceFormatSavers`  themselves. If I have some class named `ExampleLoader` that extends `ResouceFormatLoader` then ANY classes referenced by `ExampleLoader` for example `ExampleResource` and cannot contain a reference to a autoload singleton. This is a recursive property.

The MRP I provided is simply the most trivial implementation capable of triggering this error. In real world projects (such as my own) this error can be far more insidious and can appear when adding a reference to an autoload singleton to a class seemingly unrelated to  `ResourceFormatLoaders` or `ResourceFormatSavers` .

For example, in my actual project I have a custom `ResourceFormatLoader` I'll call `ExampleLoader` which loads a custom resource called `ExampleResource`. This `ExampleResource` has a method which allows me to create a custom node I'll call `ExamplePlayerNode` using the contents of the resource. This seems architecturally reasonable to me and works without issue. I've even seen a few Godot tutorials recommending something like this.

```
# Example class reference hierarchy
ExampleLoader -> ExampleResource -> ExamplePlayerNode -> ExampleWeaponNode -> Autoload
```

However, if I were to then add a reference to an autoload singleton to `ExamplePlayerNode` or even to a class referenced by `ExamplePlayerNode` such as `ExampleWeaponNode`. I'd trigger this bug and encounter a `Identifier not found: Autoload` error, despite that fact that `ExampleLoader` never calls any code related to `ExamplePlayerNode` or `ExampleWeaponNode` let alone the `Autoload` itself.

I completely agree that autoload singletons have no business anywhere in a `ResourceFormatLoaders` or `ResourceFormatSavers`  class or even a `Resource` for that matter. But adding a reference to a seemingly unrelated class should at least trigger a more fitting error message then `Identifier not found: Autoload`.

I'd be happy to provide a more detailed project file than the MRP that shows how this bug can arise in a more complex environment such as the one described here.

Perhaps a better fix would be to register autoload singletons to the language server first. Then load all custom  `ResourceFormatLoaders` and `ResourceFormatSavers` then load the autoload singletons themselves. This might fix the issue without breaking the use of custom resources in autoload singletons.

> do you know what is it about the project in particular that causes it to hit all these bugs?

I really wish I could tell you some byzantian tale of how your project is especially complex. But in this case the particular PRs that were just reverted were just completely ill-conceived. I made a mistake.

For the rest of your project, the main thing that's complex about your project is that you load things from custom resources in _load, this just causes a lot of dependencies and circular dependencies that "build up" later.

The best advice I can give you is to move as many instances of preload() in your gdscript to load() as pssible, that is where the most brittle code lies right now. Threaded loading in combination with preload() is iffy, you should really use either, not both for the foreseeable future

@max99x I accidentally edit your prior comment, I restored it back to how it was. My apologies.
author: hpvb

body: @hpvb Thanks! The project uses almost no `preload()`s (just a couple of materials, leftover from ancient code). There are a few hundred `load()s`, but the vast majority of resources (thousands) all go through a single autoload script that sends out `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request()`s in stages starting one frame after autoloads are initialized (doing it on the same frame causes all kinds of explosions). Although I explicitly cache/coalesce `load_threaded_request()` calls for the same resource, many of these calls end up being for resources that were loaded as dependencies earlier. I've never used subthreads because that has never worked for me, even though I'd love to get the speedup. There are no explicit circular dependencies as the editor wouldn't even allow it, but there are definitely implicit ones. Is there a safer way to approach it?
author: max99x

body:
> Is there a safer way to approach it?

I think, if you don't have any preloads left now you're fine.. The current version of the resource loader should work fine with what you're doing.

Edit: to clarify: the circular dependencies aren't necessarily in your resources. But because of the way the requests arrive at the loader the circular dependencies occur between resource loader threads. 

Previously that was fatal, now that should just work! But not if you end up preloading Gdscript of any kind! That's still broken (and was broken in 4.6 as well)

body:
Since we're already using AI, i gave up and asked one myself... Found the issue way faster than me 😅

So in short, `peers` is non-owned to give the client the opportunity to deref a peer. Upon destruction, the peer then deletes itself from the server's registry. If the server owned the peer, it would never destruct, and nobody would clean it up.

This is the part of my code that broke this: [github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111965/changes#diff-4f3ed5a929ee9fd3b727c691681afc33f83a0021cbc2137e19e51144935fbb52L193-L199](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111965/changes#diff-4f3ed5a929ee9fd3b727c691681afc33f83a0021cbc2137e19e51144935fbb52L193-L199)

(`pending` previously destructed, `peers` not).

The correct fix is to revert to non-owning behavior. Minimally, this looks like circumventing the hard-earned https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111965 through a direct `::new` call, similar to `ClassDB::instantiate`. This should restore pre-dev3 behavior.
A different solution might be to explicitly make the ref weak. But that's a refactor i don't feel comfortable doing, not knowing this part of the codebase very well.

I'll make a PR with the minimal reversal fix.

body:
I can confirm this on 4.7.rc eb03ae8fc (Linux) on the 2D platformer demo. On that demo:

- Open `game_singleplayer.tscn` and another scene like `coin.tscn`.
- Open `game.gd` in the script editor.
- Switch to the 2D tab, switch to `coin.tscn` then back to `game_singleplayer.tscn`.
- Notice how it switches to the Script tab. This does not occur on subsequent scene changes, until you close the script and reopen it.
- Before switching back-and-forth from/to the scene, selecting any other node that has a script attached can also cause this to happen on the first scene change (try this with the Player node in `game_singleplayer.tscn`, having `player.gd` open the script editor).

This occurs the first time you open a script in the editor, then switch back to a scene whose root node has the script attached. To reproduce the issue again, close both the scenes and scripts, then reopen them.

Bisecting it now.

**Edit:** I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116905. cc @KoBeWi

body:
For this particular issue someone would need to create its own material just for the `EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin::ON_TOP` state of the gizmo which is currently not covered because there is no material for it in the server debug.

More Info:

That editor debug is not fully controlled by the gizmo, the material is the shared server material that has xray and color from the project settings. The runtime debug is coming from the actual node and uses the same material and settings.

To be clear, there are two separated debug renderers for obstacles.

The one in the editor that included editing handles and points is rendered by the actual gizmo obstacle plugin found in `modules\navigation_3d\editor\navigation_obstacle_3d_editor_plugin`. That one checks if the gizmo is selected and not in a HIDDEN state before drawing anything, else it clears. Aka only the selected node gizmo should still be visible when the overall gizmo state is HIDDEN else you would not see editing handles.

The one that renders at runtime with debug navigation hint is more permanent and rendered by the NavigationObstacle3D node directly and uses the NavigationServer3D debug materials and properties. it also uses the ProjectSetting debug material and settings but those are only loaded at the start, for later changes a script is needed that calls the server api. Any editor change, including gizmo toggles and "game mode" overlay, that happens while that runtime is going is irrelevant for this runtime debug because the editor does not forward those changes to the runtime instance.

In the end this is just the ancient old issue that the debug is not centralized and done by the server, see proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7208. Instead editor does its own thing and because editor does not exist in the runtime the runtime needs to also do its own thing. Since the editor does not forward many changes or has callbacks for them both the server and nodes are not aware what the editor is doing.

body:
>  i expect _integrate_forces to have full collision information and full physics manipulation in the current frame

That is a misunderstanding what that function is, how physics syncs,  and how physics nodes and queries function in general.

The `_integrate_forces()` is a callback function for custom body state changes only.
When calling that callback function the PhysicsServer is in an otherwise locked state busy preparing the next iteration.

When you query the physics space in physics process you always do this before the sync and iteration update starts.
So what you really query is the physics snapshot from the last engine loop as the new has not even been build yet.

Physics nodes never update their server objects instantly, they all queue the update to be flushed and consumed in the PhysicsServer sync phase at the very begin of each physics process step. So when you do any unrelated to body state changes in that callback function all you really do is queue property updates for later.

Tried re-creating an MRP and I can't reproduce it unfortunately. Any ideas on how to proceed?

After running the engine in verbose mode and printing it out in a log, the engine hasn't finished loading the dependency before resolving the dependents, and this seems to occur only in custom resources that have as an exported variable inherited scenes.

My project is rather complicated (a few gigabytes) so I'm not sure I can replicate the exact steps easily.

I'll try to explain it without becoming pedantic.

There is an abstract class called "Seal_Class", and when I open the project in the editor, in the log it shows that it's trying to load it.

Loading resource: res://Unit/seal_class.tscn remapped: res://Unit/seal_class.tscn

body: Adding a link to this comment which actually mentions part of the cause, which is meshes with low poly counts have more inaccurate shadows. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108219#pullrequestreview-2983649861 Example: Box meshes with no subdivision Box meshes with 3 subdivisions on the long axes.

author: clayjohn

body:
To clarify, how many subdivisions you need to use depends on the size of the BoxMesh and the area covered by the AreaLight3D. Small boxes only need 1 subdivision while a huge box might need 10 or more. The distortion is applied on a per-vertex basis, which is why it becomes more accurate at higher subdivision counts.

See the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/lights_and_shadows.html#area-light
) for details.

To get accurate shadows from area lights without needing to subdivide some meshes or bake lightmaps (with the light in Static bake mode), we'd need raytraced shadows which are more precise, but also much more demanding.

body:
I think this might be by design? The documentation for `DirectionalLight2D`'s `max_distance` says
> The maximum distance from the camera center objects can be before their shadows are culled (in pixels). Decreasing this value can prevent objects located outside the camera from casting shadows (while also improving performance). Camera2D.zoom is not taken into account by max_distance, which means that at higher zoom values, shadows will appear to fade out sooner when zooming onto a given point.

Have you tried increasing the `max_distance` value?

body:
Ran into this one today, took a peek at some of the code to see if there was some sort of workaround I could employ (I haven't found one yet).

But I think I'm following the timeline of changes here:

- before multitouch support was added to BaseButton, buttons simply didn't respond to touch inputs at all, so no problems with duplicate events.

- multitouch support was added to make them respond to touch inputs, but to fix the duplicate event issue an early return statement was added to throw out emulated events.

- of course this now broke all emulated events that were sent through parse_input_event, so that was then patched up by removing the early return statement, but now it is susceptible to being hit by multiple events again!

- there was an attempt to fix this by ignoring emulated touch events, however on mobile the touch events are true, but the mouse events are emulated, so that doesn't prevent duplicates... and you can't fix it by also throwing out emulated mouse events because that would just kick the issue back to the previous broken state...

All that said, I have no idea how to actually fix this, any solution I can think of would be really hacky... personally I'm gonna just roll my project back to 4.6 for now.
author: ace24713

body:
I looked into this and have a fix ready.

The duplicate `pressed` emission happens because touch input with mouse emulation enabled can deliver two GUI paths to `BaseButton`: first the touch-generated mouse event, then the original screen touch event. My first pass guarded the direct mouse-button path, but there was one extra edge to cover: if `ui_accept` can match the touch-emulated mouse button event, that event may still go through the action path and the real touch event can emit again.

The fix I prepared marks mouse button/motion events generated from touch, preserves that marker through event transforms, and has `BaseButton` ignore those touch-emulated mouse events for the mouse-button, mouse-motion, and `ui_accept` paths. Ordinary emulated mouse events are still accepted, so this should not reintroduce the earlier `Input.parse_input_event()` regression.

I also added regression tests for:
- touch input with mouse emulation only emitting `pressed` once,
- the `ui_accept` edge case,
- ordinary emulated mouse events still triggering buttons.

I've already opened a PR to fix this issue

body:
- Can reproduce, probably caused by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115980

It happens in floating docks too, not just the ScriptEditor.

The previous behavior was a bug, inputs from floating windows should not be sent to the main window.
If you make a scene with a Window, you will see it is normal that inputs in the child Window do not get sent to the parent.

However in the editor, you can use `_shortcut_input` to get events from child windows, if they haven't been accepted already.
Otherwise, the best way I know to get inputs from child windows is to find each Window that you care about and connect to all of their `window_input` signals.

As mentioned by @AThousandShips , the scale documentation notes this is expected behaviour with negative x scales. If you are just trying to flip the sprite as you move backwards, [`Sprite2D.flip_h`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d-property-flip-h) is probably the better option.

For the general issue of scale with Physics bodies, see [Troubleshooting physics issues: Scaled physics bodies or collision shapes do not collide correctly](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/troubleshooting_physics_issues.html#scaled-physics-bodies-or-collision-shapes-do-not-collide-correctly). body: @zongo811 No worries, essentially properties like `scale`, `rotation` and `position` are mapped on to a transformation matrix which is used for calculations ([`Transform2D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_transform2d.html#class-transform2d)). What the `scale` docs are saying is that because of how scale is encoded in this transform, a negative x-scale cannot be extracted back out as it is equivalent to a different interpretation which is prioritised (probably since it is more common).

> Is there another way to get a debug-enabled build of Godot without building it myself?

@Pixelmusement You can download the artifacts zip I built with Actions, or you can fork [my actions repository](https://github.com/saierXP/Godot-Custom-Build-Templates) to enable the free GitHub Actions function.

https://github.com/saierXP/Godot-Custom-Build-Templates/actions/runs/28568715878
Create a `run.bat` command file in the same path and replace `project_path` with your project path. After running, a `log.txt` file will be generated to record the crash message.
```bat
@echo off
rem Force search for debugging symbols in pdb under the same path.
set _NT_SYMBOL_PATH=%~dp0;SRV*C:\Symbols*https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols

rem replace to your project folder path
set project_path=""

"%~dp0godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.exe" -e --path "%project_path%"  2> "%~dp0log.txt"

pause >nul
```

Caused by Godot’s splash screen theme + screenOrientation="portrait".

2.- GPU / Native crash (rare, on very old hardware):
SIGSEGV at garbage addresses (like 0xff00ff00),
typical of broken/old Mali GPU drivers + memory corruption on ancient devices.

Classic problems of supporting very old Android versions.
However it's true they concentrated on Android 8.0 and some 8.1 devices.

No direct problems with Android 7 and below, but very few Android 7 users ever installed/tried the app anyway..

In any case, raising the Min SDK bar to 27 has been positive for my app,
99% of crashes are gone now, and there's still a good 16K+ compatible devices.. (16,633 to be exact..)

https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/s/ZpapD8ytiR to repeat

There are a few complicating factors.

It seems like your StateMachine for the `right` state isn't complete.

You also have a code flaw

	func is_walking_right() -> bool:

should be

	func is_walking_right() -> bool:

What's happening in the MRP is the StateMachine is flowing immediately to the `right` from a `stand`. I'm not totally sure why this throws an error. But fixing this in code resolves that specific MRP ZIP.

I can't get the same error if is_walking_left is altered to 

	return speed <= 0.0

So there may be something wrong specifically with `right` animation.

body:
I don't consider this a breaking change. The previous behaviour was broken and the code in question added an error message to explain that the code was broken. 

In general bug fixes are not considered breaking changes since doing so would flood the migration doc. However, some bug fixes are considered breaking changes, especially if they change the behaviour of features that were working previous to the bug fix. 

This PR adds a guard across behaviour that is invalid. If anyone hits the error its because their code is buggy and needs to be fixed. In that way the error is a sort of self-documenting mechanism. You don't need to be notified that the error may occur. It automatically gets printed for any user that needs to see if. 

Therefore, I wouldn't document this change as a breaking change.

For example, if a node holds a reference to instance A, which directly or indirectly holds a reference back to A, A's reference count will be 2. body:
Good news: that test confirmed it, and the fix turned out to be tiny.

Plain-English version of what was happening: Godot 4.7 updated the library it uses to hand out video memory, and the new version added a stricter limit check. On AMD integrated graphics that limit is low, so once your project loads enough textures and meshes it trips the check and the engine starts refusing to create anything else; that's the wall of errors and the crash. NVIDIA cards have a vastly higher limit, which is why nobody on those saw it. Switching that one check back off restores the 4.6 behavior.

I've put up a one-line fix, plus a build with just that change so you can confirm it before it goes through review:
https://github.com/vorvek/godot/releases/tag/vma-maxalloc-fix-120534

Open the project the same way; it should just work now.

---

**For the team (technical detail):**

Root cause is the VMA 3.1.0 to 3.3.0 bump (805c9d4b18), which pulled in upstream VMA [`89d3a6a`](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/commit/89d3a6a5ea35d140fe865ed493c89bde777c6a07): it flips `VMA_DEBUG_DONT_EXCEED_MAX_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_COUNT` from `0` to `1`. VMA then returns `VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS` (the `-10`) once the live `VkDeviceMemory` count hits `maxMemoryAllocationCount` instead of forwarding to the driver. AMD iGPUs report a low count (4096) and this project crosses it on load; NVIDIA's is ~4 billion, hence AMD-only, and D3D12 is unaffected.

It isn't a leak on Godot's side; RD RID counts stay flat/small (confirmed with a probe build). The renderer simply makes >4096 distinct allocations on these GPUs, which 4.6 (VMA 3.1.0, macro `= 0`) tolerated by letting the driver service them. Fix in #120603 defines the macro back to `0`.

I'm also closing my earlier #120573; it cached descriptor sets, but the logs here show every failure is device-memory allocation, not descriptor allocation, so it was aimed at the wrong layer.

body:
It looks like metal copy-queue staging buffer overflow (alignment applied after the copy). I backtraced my project and found this lines:

```
#7  -[MTLDebugBlitCommandEncoder copyFromBuffer:sourceOffset:toBuffer:destinationOffset:size:]  ← Metal ABORTS here
#9  MTL::BlitCommandEncoder::copyFromBuffer(sourceOffset=65544, destinationOffset=0, size=8)
#10 RenderingDeviceDriverMetal::_copy_queue_copy_to_buffer(p_src_data=(_len=8), p_dst_offset=0)   rendering_device_driver_metal.cpp:2488
```

Watch the offset approach the 64 KB edge. Say offset = 65528, and a copy of size = 8 comes in (your arg-buffer copy):

1. available = 65536 − 65528 = 8. Check: 8 < 8? No → no flush.
2. memcpy + blit at offset 65528, 8 bytes → uses bytes 65528–65535. In bounds, fine.
3. consume(8): aligned = round_up(65528, 16) = 65536, then offset = 65536 + 8 =  65544. Boom

body:
I have noticed the following annoying behavior (first noticed in 4.6.3, also present in 4.7):

- Have two scenes, scene B instantiated inside of scene A
- With both scenes open, save the scene B (no actual changes to the scene needed)
- Then switch to scene A, this triggers an update of the instances (which I suspect is the culprit)
- All resources appear as duplicated

It goes away by switching to B and back to A again without saving. Or in general switching between scenes or closing them and opening them again.

This happens with all resources, even resources not shared between the scenes. Doing the same steps but without one scene instantiated inside the other does not cause the issue (and does not cause an update of the instances). Saving the scene that has instances of the other, and switching does not cause the issue. The problem happens specifically if we save an scene that has instances in another scene, and then switch to that other scene.

This happens even without custom resource types or scripts. I have been able to reproduce it with two scenes, each an static body with collision shape, the shape will appear duplicated.

I also tested if this is affected by the scene thumbnails, disabling the thumbnails does not have an impact on the issue.

There is no warning or error output associated with the bug.

For the impact, I'll say that our designer has got into the habit of always clicking the indicator to duplicate the resources. There is no real harm except when accidentally duplicating a resource that is saved to file.

body: I investigated this issue a little bit further and this is what I discovered: * The same scene (with `Basis Universal` compression enabled) fully works on mobile devices (at least it does on my iPhone) * Turns out, `Basis Universal` compression for Web works, but only if the compressed texture's resolution is a power of 4 After googling the problem a coupe of times I found out, that `Basis Universal` uses BC compression format for desktop platforms, which requires texture's resolution to be a power of 4 Mobile platforms use different compression format which doesn't pose this requirement

body:
The resolution being a multiple of the block size (4 in this case) is a requirement for all compressed formats, actually. WebGL often doesn't allow setting the resolution to a different value than the texture's actual size (#104260). The workaround works since the code for padding the textures is kind of broken (it only pads them if the texture has mipmaps). 

#113185 should fix this and a bunch of other issues, if you are able to test it please let me know if it works.

In the meantime, I'm working on a smaller fix that can be backported to 4.7

body: That is because change in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90644 sets the custom debug color and fill option on every single collision shape when the shape resource is set. Each of those newer debug setters forces a shape update and clear of the debug mesh cache and a changed signal emit. So especially a tool script ends up updating the debug shape over and over and over and convex shapes have a costly point-to-hull calculation on top.
author: smix8

body: Okay, is there something else to do other than updating the scenes/code to hide the shapes?
author: solodeveloping

body: There is no simple solution here because the debug mesh cache that does all the performance costly things is inside the Shape3D resource and gets triggered on setters everytime that Resource is used. It just happen to be used by anything that tries to render the debug mesh but it also happens everytime a new Node instance tries to call the resource setters like the CollisionObject3D does when entering the tree. Inside the Editor there is also the gizmo that does the actual rendering and not the node. So both the editor debug, the runtime debug, and the shape resource need to be fixed in that regard to avoid unnecessary performance problems when the debug is not visible.

body: it's happening because "unsigned int last_mouse_monitor_mask" at 212 line of display_server_x11 header is always 0 at the start of the engine. This triggers "if (mask != last_mouse_monitor_mask)" at 4839 line of "display_server_x11.cpp" because the mask is never equal zero. Only after this last_mouse_monitor_mask gets updated which prevents those closures later So I did add check if the last_mouse_monitor_mask is zero and if so, we set this value to current mask value and that fixed the problem @bluebirdsan, can you add to the topic that it's related only to x11 server? Because I suppose that on the wayland it's already a different bug and PR docs recommend to bring only one change at the time

body:
```
vec3 v = vec3(false); <-- won't compile
vec3 v = vec3(float(false)); <-- works as expected
```
Imo this is not a bug, this should be the behaviour. Trying to create a `vec3` from a `bool` should be a bug in 99% of cases, and when you want to do it deliberately, you can cast.

Why do you think this is a bug?
author: lawnjelly

body:
imo it is a bug because it is a significant difference from expected glsl behaviour and would prevent copying glsl directly to gdshader for no beneficial reason. Since the language is strictly typed, there's not really any way you can do this by accident either. C++ converts bool to int and vice versa implicitly as well. 

I write a lot of glsl, and discovered this discrepancy my first day writing shaders in Godot so I'd say it's worth fixing. It's quite useful for quickly testing conditions, and I have never experienced a bug from this behaviour.

I may be biased because for me, glsl is almost the perfect language, and gdshader subtly improves on its limitations. It would be a tremendous shame for it to lose any functionality.
author: ahs3n

body: I guess if glsl does this natively, that is a decent argument to supporting them I guess (although I personally prefer explicit).
author: lawnjelly

body: There's also an argument to be made that `vec3(true)` actually _is_ explicit because a `vecN` is always float and only float. There's `ivecN` and `bvecN` for integers and booleans respectively

Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).

- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

body:
Thanks for putting up a PR for the warning @VewDev - I couldn't find anything on it during my searches, so nice find.

It's an odd decision from my point of view. I imagine for someone making a game with resolution changes and having to test that their code works completely from end to end, they'd have to generate a game build each time they wanted to test it and go through the flow. Pretty tedious I imagine and I think the old setting of just having the embedded window 'black out' the corners to indicate the resolution change would be preferred, personally.
